chunks: I heard him saying: “When the obligatory prayer becomes due, then begin with it; and it does not harm you to leave the supererogatory prayer that comes before it.”

And what you have also presented of the reports stating that the beginning of the time is more virtuous confirms these reports. So how do you reconcile between these and those? We say: as for what is contained in the reports that we cited earlier—that prayer at the beginning of the time is more virtuous—it is to be understood as referring to the time that comes after the time of the supererogatory prayer. For supererogatory prayers may only be performed in advance until the passing of the measure of two feet or one cubit; once that measure has passed, it is not permissible to occupy oneself with the supererogatory prayers. Rather, one should begin with the obligatory prayer, and that time is more virtuous than the time after it, which is the time of one under constraint and the people of excuses. We have already cited the reports concerning all of that, and what he narrated further clarifies it:
Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Khālid and ʿUbays ibn Hishām, from Thābit, from Ziyād ibn Abī Ghiyāth, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.أَوَّلَ الْوَقْتِ: the beginning portion of the prayer time, regarded as more virtuous
key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: the supererogatory prayer performed in addition to the obligatory prayer
key_terms.الْأَعْذَارِ: excuses or valid impediments affecting the timing of prayer
key_terms.الْفَرْضِ: the obligatory duty, here the prescribed prayer
key_terms.الْمُضْطَرِّ: one under constraint who delays to a later time out of necessity

ai.seo_question: When the time of the obligatory salat (prayer) arrives, should one continue the nafilah or begin the obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This passage explains that when the time of the obligatory salat (prayer) arrives, it takes precedence over the preceding supererogatory prayer. It also reconciles reports about the virtue of praying at the beginning of the time by clarifying that this virtue applies after the permitted window for the nafilah has passed, after which one should begin with the obligatory prayer.
